eyebrow: Annual in-service
title: Emergency Preparedness Beyond Fire
subtitle: For staff at Pennsylvania personal care homes and assisted living facilities. 55 Pa. Code 2600.65(g)(2) and 2800.65(j)(2).

eyebrow: Part one
title: The first sixty seconds, before you know what this is

eyebrow: In this order, every time
title: What you do before you understand it
points: Look. Is anyone in danger right now?
Say it out loud — get one other person moving
Go to your assignment, not toward the noise
Account for the residents you are responsible for
Report what you saw, not what you concluded

eyebrow: The most common mistake in a real event
quote: Everybody walks toward the noise, and a hallway nobody was assigned to goes unchecked.
attribution: Your assignment is boring and it is the whole system. Four people at the interesting end of the building is four rooms nobody opened.

eyebrow: A resident collapses, or somebody is at the door
title: When a second emergency lands inside the first
points: Your role does not change because the night did
Notify — do not investigate, and do not go look
A medical event still gets the nurse, not you
Security: distance, doors, and tell somebody
Never leave your assignment to go help elsewhere

eyebrow: Part two
title: Staying put, or moving — and what moving actually costs

eyebrow: Somebody above you makes this call
title: The two options, and what each needs
points: Shelter: interior rooms, away from glass
Shelter: bring water, meds, the resident list
Evacuate: horizontal first — past fire doors
Evacuate: down a floor only if you must
Either way: count before, and count after

eyebrow: Be honest about the arithmetic
quote: Moving a building full of people with walkers takes longer than the warning gives you.
attribution: Start early and stand down if you were wrong. Standing down costs an apology. Starting late costs something else.

eyebrow: Part three
title: The utilities, and who they take down with them

eyebrow: It is never just the lights
title: What leaves when the power leaves
points: Oxygen concentrators, CPAPs, feeding pumps
Heat, cooling, and the medication fridge
Elevators, and the electronic door locks
Call bells, in a lot of buildings
The computer holding your resident list

eyebrow: Find this out tonight, not that night
quote: Which outlets does your generator actually come back on?
attribution: That single fact is the difference between an oxygen concentrator that keeps running and one that does not. Almost nobody can answer it until the night it matters.

eyebrow: Part four
title: The residents this is hardest on

eyebrow: Dark, loud, crowded, strangers
title: Why an emergency hits dementia hardest
points: Alarms and radios remove what little quiet helped
Flashlights in a dark hall read as threat
Strangers in gear are not recognizable as help
Being rushed is the fastest way to lose them
One familiar face beats four efficient ones

eyebrow: Know these people by name, now
title: Who needs power to stay well
points: Oxygen — and how many hours the tank buys
CPAP, ventilator, suction
Feeding pumps and IV pumps
Refrigerated medication, insulin especially
Anyone whose lift is electric

eyebrow: Part five
title: The count, and the things that go up the chain

eyebrow: The most valuable thing you can hand a responder
quote: An unexplained empty bed gets treated as a person still inside.
attribution: So report the resident at the podiatrist by name and where she is. Otherwise crews search a room for somebody who was never in the building.

eyebrow: The hardest instruction in this course
quote: Do not call families, and do not post anything.
attribution: Privacy does not take the night off. Notification comes from administration so every family gets the same true thing, instead of six half-versions from six people.

eyebrow: Part six
title: When it does not end in an hour

eyebrow: Hour three is a different problem
title: What a long event turns into
points: Meals, medications, and toileting still come due
Backup oxygen runs down on its own schedule
The relief shift may not be able to get in
You will be tired, and tired people skip counts
Say early that you are running out of something

eyebrow: What a drill is actually for
quote: The silent drill where everything went fine is the one that lied to you.
attribution: The stuck door, the dead flashlight, the out-of-date list — say all of it in the debrief. That is the drill doing its job, not complaining.

eyebrow: What to carry out of this course
quote: How this goes depends far less on the binder than on what the person standing in that hallway already knows.
attribution: Tonight that is you. Know your building, know who needs something to stay alive, and know your assignment.
